title: QUIZ - 20
description: Test your knowledge, strengthen your reasoning, and learn something new with every question.

questions.concept: Finding the Constant of Direct Proportionality
questions.learningObjective: Determine the constant of proportionality from a direct variation relationship
questions.question: A quantity y varies directly with x. When x = 15, y = 150. What is the constant of proportionality k (where y = kx)?
questions.hint: For direct proportionality y = kx, the constant k equals y divided by x.

questions.concept: Predicting Values Using Direct Proportionality
questions.learningObjective: Use a known direct-proportion pair to predict a new value
questions.question: The amount of paint needed varies directly with the wall area. If x = 5 gives y = 45, what is y when x = 10?
questions.explanation: Since y varies directly with x, y/x is constant: 45/5 = 9. So when \(x = 10, y = 9 \times 10 = 90\).
questions.hint: In direct proportionality, y/x stays constant, so find k first, then multiply by the new x.

questions.concept: Recognizing Direct Proportion from a Table
questions.learningObjective: Determine whether a table of values represents a direct proportion
questions.question: Does the following set of (x, y) pairs represent a direct proportion? (1, 5), (2, 10), (3, 15), (4, 20)

options.label: A
options.text: No, because y/x is not the same for every pair.

options.label: B
options.text: Yes, because y increases as x increases.

options.label: C
options.text: It cannot be determined from a table of values.

options.label: D
options.text: Yes, because y/x is the same constant value for every pair.

questions.explanation: Checking y/x for each pair: 5/1 = 5, 10/2 = 5, 15/3 = 5, 20/4 = 5. These ratios are all equal, confirming a direct proportion.
questions.hint: A direct proportion requires y/x to be the same constant for every pair of values.

questions.concept: Recognizing Direct Proportion from a Table

questions.question: Does the following set of (x, y) pairs represent a direct proportion? (1, 5), (2, 8), (3, 14), (4, 29)

options.label: B

options.label: D
